_what_this_is: The load-sensitive assertions FITWAY has independently observed going red inside a single pnpm verify:full invocation and green when their suite is run standalone at the same commit. It exists so a verifier does not pay for four full ladder runs to re-derive a failure someone else already recorded, and it is not a licence: scripts/flaky-attribution-check.mjs fails closed on anything unlisted, on an entry with one uncorroborated observation, on an entry opened by the session reporting the failure, on a candidate that touches the entry's surface, and on a missing standalone re-run. One unlisted failing assertion makes the whole run red.
_provenance: Entries transcribed from evidence recorded by earlier sessions, not opened by the session that first used this file. The b01 independent verifier recorded all three locations in docs/phase-records/handoffs/phase11-access/20260822-173000-p11_access_b01-failed-validation.md, together with the standalone 83/83 pass at the same commit. The phase2 integration entry was named at the S4 close.

entries.title: locally expires cached fresh JSON without another request
entries.mechanism: A cache-expiry timing assertion. Inside a single verify:full invocation the browser step runs after build, unit, and integration on the same machine, and the elapsed-time margin this assertion depends on is compressed under that load.

observations.result: red inside verify:full, green standalone 83/83 at the same commit

entries.title: History exposes prerequisite pending, error, and one deliberate retry chain
entries.mechanism: Asserts a transient loading state is visible. Under load the transition completes before the assertion samples it, so the element is not found rather than wrong.
